# Open Software Source Code Distribution

This repository provides source code for licensed software components used in NVIDIA diagnostic tools, in compliance
with OSS license requirements.

## Available Source Code

| Package | Version | Archive File | License | Source |
|---------|---------|--------------|---------|---------|
| GCC | 12.2.0 | `gcc-12.2.0.tar.xz` | GPLv3 | https://gcc.gnu.org/mirrors.html |
| Python | 3.10.7 | `Python-3.10.7.tgz` | PSF | https://www.python.org/downloads/source/ |
| Python | 3.10.19 | `Python-3.10.19.tgz` | PSF | https://www.python.org/downloads/source/ |
| Paramiko | 3.1.0 | `paramiko-3.1.0.tar.gz` | LGPL | https://github.com/paramiko/paramiko |
| Paramiko | 3.5.1 | `paramiko-3.5.1.tar.gz` | LGPL | https://github.com/paramiko/paramiko |
| Pylint | 3.0.3 | `v3.0.3.tar.gz` | GPL | https://github.com/pylint-dev/pylint |
| Python Astroid | 3.0.3 | `astroid-3.0.3.tar.gz` | LGPL | https://github.com/pylint-dev/astroid |

## License Information

Each source code archive contains complete license documentation. Please refer to the files within each archive for specific license terms and conditions.

## Purpose

This repository exists solely to fulfill OSS source code distribution requirements.

---

## Security

NVIDIA is dedicated to the security and trust of our software products and services, including all source code repositories managed through our organization.

If you need to report a security issue, please use the appropriate contact points outlined below. **Please do not report security vulnerabilities through GitHub.**

## Reporting Potential Security Vulnerability in an NVIDIA Product

To report a potential security vulnerability in any NVIDIA product:
- Web: [Security Vulnerability Submission Form](https://www.nvidia.com/object/submit-security-vulnerability.html)
- E-Mail: psirt@nvidia.com
    - We encourage you to use the following PGP key for secure email communication: [NVIDIA public PGP Key for communication](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/security/pgp-key)
    - Please include the following information:
   	 - Product/Driver name and version/branch that contains the vulnerability
     - Type of vulnerability (code execution, denial of service, buffer overflow, etc.)
   	 - Instructions to reproduce the vulnerability
   	 - Proof-of-concept or exploit code
   	 - Potential impact of the vulnerability, including how an attacker could exploit the vulnerability

While NVIDIA currently does not have a bug bounty program, we do offer acknowledgement when an externally reported security issue is addressed under our coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy. Please visit our [Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT)](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/security/psirt-policies/) policies page for more information.

## NVIDIA Product Security

For all security-related concerns, please visit NVIDIA's Product Security portal at https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/security
